decisions.choice: and said to them: the start of Moses' second speech
decisions.reason: A short narrative line introduces Moses' words, which begin with "Hear, Israel" and run without a break to 26:19. The first speech ended at 4:40, and 4:44-49 described the setting. This second speech holds the ten words (verses 6-21) and the laws of chapters 12-26.

decisions.choice: statutes and judgments: the laws and the rulings Moses is about to teach
decisions.reason: The pair names the whole body of law as fixed rules (statutes) and decisions for cases (judgments), as in 4:1, 5 and 4:45. Verse 31 adds "the commandment" and says Moses received all of it from God at Horeb.

decisions.choice: speaking in your ears: speaking to you directly, so that you hear it
decisions.reason: To speak "in someone's ears" is to say it aloud in their hearing (31:28, 30; Genesis 23:13). Moses stresses that the people hear it from him in person today.

decisions.choice: learn them and keep them, to do them: hearing leads to learning, and learning to doing
decisions.reason: The three verbs form a chain that runs through Deuteronomy: hear, learn, keep, do (4:1, 10; 6:1-3; 31:12). "Keep" means to watch over, take care, and with "to do" it means to be careful to carry the laws out.

decisions.choice: Listen, Israel!
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word "listen" here. The same call opens 6:4, where every level keeps "Hear, Israel".

decisions.choice: "Escucha" (singular), then plural forms ("{{plural_you:aprenderán|aprenderéis}}")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls Israel as one and goes on in the plural; Spanish follows the Hebrew number, as throughout Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: the narrator's line in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("appela", "convoqua", "dit") and the passé composé at Readable ("a rassemblé", "a dit"); Moses' speech in the tenses of speech
decisions.reason: As set for Deuteronomy at 1:1. Only this opening line is narration; from "Écoute, Israël" on, Moses speaks, and his retelling of Horeb is in the passé composé at every level.

decisions.choice: "Écoute" (singular), then "vous" (plural)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls Israel as one ("hear" is singular) and goes on in the plural ("your ears", "you will learn"). French follows the Hebrew number, as throughout Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: "Sikia" (L, B), "Sikiliza" (R), singular; then plural ("mtajifunza", "jifunzeni")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls Israel as one and goes on in the plural; Swahili follows the Hebrew number. "Sikia" (hear) is kept at Literal and Balanced, as in the call that opens 6:4; Readable says "Sikiliza" (listen), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "nói vào tai các ngươi" (L)
decisions.reason: To speak in someone's ears is to speak to them directly (meaning decision); Vietnamese "nói vào tai" can keep the picture at Literal, while Balanced and Readable say "công bố cho", "nói cho ... biết".

decisions.choice: not with our fathers, but with us: the covenant binds this generation directly
alternatives: not only with our fathers, but also with us
not with the patriarchs, but with us
decisions.reason: Most of the adults who stood at Horeb had died in the wilderness (2:14-16), and many who now listen were children then. Moses insists that the covenant was made with them, not as something handed down from the past. The "fathers" may be that dead generation, and then the saying means "not only with them, but with us", a way of speaking that puts all the weight on the second part. Or the fathers may be the patriarchs (4:31, 37; 7:8, 12), with whom God swore a covenant but to whom he did not give this one, and then the saying is meant just as it stands.

decisions.choice: with us, we, these here today, all of us living: heaped-up emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew piles up words for the people present: "us", "we", "these", "here", "today", "all of us", "living". Each one presses the point that the covenant is theirs.

decisions.choice: with us, we, these [who are] here
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated pronoun so the reader can see the emphasis (m2); Balanced and Readable carry it with "the ones here today, all of us" and "every one of us".

decisions.choice: face to face: directly, in person, not through a messenger
decisions.reason: The phrase means that God himself spoke and the people heard his voice (verses 22-24; 4:12, 33, 36). It does not mean they saw him: they saw no form, only fire (4:12, 15). Exodus 33:11 and Numbers 12:8 use similar words of Moses alone; here the whole people heard the ten words for themselves.

decisions.choice: from the midst of the fire: the fire on the mountain at Horeb
decisions.reason: The mountain burned with fire when God came down on it (4:11; Exodus 19:18). Deuteronomy repeats that God spoke "from the midst of the fire" (4:12, 15, 33, 36; verses 22-26).

decisions.choice: directly

ko.L: 그때에 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}와 너희 사이에 서서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀을 너희에게 전했다. 너희가 불 때문에 두려워하여 산에 올라가지 않았기 때문이다. 그분께서 말씀하셨다.

vi.R: Hồi đó tôi đã đứng giữa {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và anh em. Tôi ở đó để nói cho anh em biết những gì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán, vì anh em sợ lửa và không dám lên núi. Đây là những lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán:

decisions.choice: saying: introduces the words God spoke, picking up verse 4
decisions.reason: Verse 5 is an aside about Moses' part in the events. The word "saying" at its end does not introduce words of Moses; it goes back to "Yahweh spoke with you" in verse 4 and opens God's own words in verses 6-21.

decisions.choice: standing between: Moses as the go-between for God and the people
decisions.reason: The people heard God's voice (verse 4), yet Moses stood between them because they feared the fire (verses 23-27; Exodus 20:18-21). The two statements fit together: they heard the ten words themselves, and Moses carried everything else God said to them (verse 31).

decisions.choice: afraid from the face of the fire: afraid because of the fire
decisions.reason: "From the face of" is a common way of saying "because of" or "in the presence of".

decisions.choice: He said: / This is what he said:
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable end the aside and begin a new sentence, so they supply who speaks, God (m1). Literal keeps the single word "saying".

decisions.choice: the aside in brackets, then "rằng:" (L)
decisions.reason: "saying" at the end of the verse picks up "spoke" in verse 4 (meaning decision); Literal sets Moses' explanation in parentheses so that "rằng" can lead into God's words. Balanced and Readable make it a sentence of its own, as the English does.

decisions.choice: the ten words, as given in Exodus 20:2-17
decisions.reason: Moses repeats the ten words God spoke at Horeb (Exodus 20:2-17). Most of the wording is the same, but there are differences: the Sabbath is to be "kept" rather than "remembered" and is given a different reason (verses 12-15), two promises are added (verse 16), the last commands are joined by "and" (verses 18-21), and the coveting command names the wife first and adds the field (verse 21). Here the words are quoted within Moses' speech.

decisions.choice: I am Yahweh your God: God names himself before he commands
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:2, the words can also be read "I, Yahweh, am your God". Either way God first says who he is and what he has done, and the commands rest on that rescue.

decisions.choice: house of slaves: Egypt as the place of slavery
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures Egypt as a household where Israel served as slaves (6:12; 7:8; 8:14; Exodus 13:3; 20:2). Verse 15 returns to it.

decisions.choice: the ten words are counted in more than one way
decisions.reason: Scripture says there are ten (4:13; 10:4) but does not number them. Communities count them differently, as noted at Exodus 20:2; Deuteronomy's form of the last command (verse 21) is the basis of one of those counts.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" at every level, since this is Israel's slavery in Egypt, as at Exodus 20:2.

decisions.choice: the wording of Exodus 20:2-17 in Spanish, changed only where the Hebrew of Deuteronomy differs; “ ” inside Moses' speech
decisions.reason: Where the Hebrew is the same as in Exodus, the Spanish is the same, so that the real differences (the Sabbath "guardado", its reason, the coveting command) stand out.

decisions.choice: the wording of Exodus 20:2-17 in French, changed only where the Hebrew of Deuteronomy differs; “ ” for God's words inside Moses' speech
decisions.reason: The ten words are quoted inside Moses' speech, so they open with the inner quotation mark. Where the Hebrew is the same as in Exodus, the French is the same, so that a reader comparing the two sees only the real differences (the Sabbath "gardé", its reason, the coveting command).

decisions.choice: the wording of Exodus 20:2-17 in Swahili, changed only where the Hebrew of Deuteronomy differs
decisions.reason: Where the Hebrew is the same as in Exodus, the Swahili is the same, so that the real differences ("Shika" the Sabbath, its reason, the coveting command) stand out.

decisions.choice: God's ten words in 해라체 with "너" at every level, Balanced and Readable included, following the Hebrew singular
decisions.reason: God speaks in 해라체 throughout, and Readable keeps God's quoted words in that style even inside Moses' 합쇼체 address. Balanced keeps the singular "너" through the ten words, as the book-wide choice recorded at 1:21 allows for a long singular passage; the wording stays close to the Korean Exodus 20 so that the two versions can be compared, while following this text's own differences.

decisions.choice: "ngươi", singular, at every level in the ten words
decisions.reason: God speaks to Israel as one person through verse 21; Vietnamese keeps the singular "ngươi", as in Exodus 20. These are God's own words, so Moses' "anh em" does not apply inside them.

decisions.choice: on my face: besides me, in my presence
decisions.reason: The same words as Exodus 20:3. The phrase may mean "besides me", "in my presence" or "in defiance of me"; each reading forbids Israel any god but Yahweh.

decisions.choice: other gods: no rival may share Israel's loyalty
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy returns to this command again and again (6:14; 7:4; 8:19; 13:3).

decisions.choice: You shall not ... (Literal, Balanced); Do not ... (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20, the commands use the form of a lasting prohibition. Literal and Balanced say "You shall not"; Readable uses the plain "Do not".

decisions.choice: future at L and B ("no tendrás", "no harás"); negative imperative at R ("no tengas", "no hagas")
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20: the future of law at Literal and Balanced, the plain command at Readable.

decisions.choice: future with "ne ... pas" at L and B ("tu n'auras pas", "tu ne feras pas"); imperative at R ("n'aie pas", "ne fais pas")
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20. The commands are lasting prohibitions; Literal and Balanced use the French future of law, Readable the plain imperative, as the English Readable says "Do not".

decisions.choice: -ta- future with the negative ("hutakuwa", "hutafanya") or the negative subjunctive at L and B; the negative subjunctive at R ("usiwe", "usiibe")
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20: the lasting prohibition at Literal and Balanced, the plain command at Readable.

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall make for yourself a carved image, any form which [is] in the heavens above and which [is] on the earth beneath and which [is] in the waters under the earth.

en.L: You shall not make for yourself a carved image, any form that [is] in the heavens above, or that [is] on the earth beneath, or that [is] in the waters under the earth.
en.B: You shall not make yourself a carved idol in the form of anything in the heavens overhead, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.
en.R: Do not make any idol for yourself in the shape of anything in the sky, on the land, or in the water below the land.

ko.L: 너는 너를 위하여 새긴 우상을 만들지 말라. 위로 하늘에 있는 것이나 아래로 땅에 있는 것이나 땅 아래 물속에 있는 것의 어떤 형상도 [만들지 말라].

ko.R: 너를 위해 우상을 만들면 안 된다. 하늘에 있는 것이든, 땅에 있는 것이든, 땅 아래 물속에 있는 것이든, 그 어떤 것의 모양으로도 우상을 만들면 안 된다.

vi.L: Ngươi chớ làm cho mình tượng chạm, bất cứ hình dạng nào [của vật] ở trên trời cao, hay ở dưới đất thấp, hay ở trong nước dưới đất.

vi.R: Đừng làm cho mình một thần tượng nào theo hình dạng của bất cứ vật gì ở trên trời, trên mặt đất, hay ở dưới nước.

decisions.choice: a carved image, any form: an idol in the shape of anything
decisions.reason: Exodus 20:4 reads "a carved image and any form", two things forbidden. Here there is no "and", so "any form" describes the image: an idol shaped like anything in the world. The command forbids the same thing either way.

decisions.choice: no image of anything, including of Yahweh himself
decisions.reason: 4:15-18 gives the reason: Israel saw no form when Yahweh spoke from the fire, so they must make no image of anything, whether of another god or meant to stand for him.

decisions.choice: heavens, earth, waters under the earth: the whole created world
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:4, the three parts name everything there is: the birds and lights of the sky, land animals and people, and fish (4:16-19).

en.L: You shall not bow down to them, and you shall not serve them; for I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, [am] a jealous God, visiting [the] iniquity of fathers upon children, and upon [the] third and upon [the] fourth [generation] of those who hate {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}},
en.B: You shall neither bow to them nor serve them. For I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, am a jealous God. I bring the guilt of fathers upon their children, upon the third and the fourth generation of those who hate {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}},
en.R: Do not bow down to them or serve them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and I am a jealous God. I will not share your loyalty with other gods. When people hate {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I punish their sin, even in their grandchildren and great-grandchildren.

es.L: No te postrarás ante ellas, y no las servirás; porque yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, [soy] un Dios celoso, que visita la iniquidad de los padres sobre los hijos, y sobre la tercera y sobre la cuarta [generación] de los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} odian,
es.B: No te inclinarás ante ellos ni les rendirás culto. Pues yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, un Dios celoso. Hago caer la culpa de los padres sobre sus hijos, sobre la tercera y la cuarta generación de los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} odian,
es.R: No te arrodilles ante ellos ni les sirvas. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, y soy un Dios celoso: no permito que tu lealtad sea también para otros dioses. Cuando alguien {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} odia, castigo su pecado, aun en sus nietos y bisnietos.

fr.L: Tu ne te prosterneras pas devant elles, et tu ne les serviras pas ; car {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, [je suis] un Dieu jaloux, qui visite la faute des pères sur les fils, et sur la troisième et sur la quatrième [génération] de ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} haïssent,
fr.B: Tu ne t’inclineras pas devant elles et tu ne leur rendras pas de culte. Je suis en effet {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, un Dieu jaloux. Je fais retomber la faute des pères sur leurs enfants, sur la troisième et la quatrième génération de ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} haïssent,
fr.R: Ne te prosterne pas devant elles et ne les sers pas. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, et je suis un Dieu jaloux : je ne veux pas que ta fidélité soit partagée avec d’autres dieux. Quand des gens {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} haïssent, je punis leur péché, même chez leurs petits-enfants et leurs arrière-petits-enfants.

sw.L: Hutaviinamia, wala hutavitumikia; kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, [ni] Mungu mwenye wivu, ninayeadhibu uovu wa baba juu ya watoto, na juu ya [kizazi cha] tatu na juu ya [kizazi cha] nne cha wale wanaonichukia,
sw.B: Hutaviinamia wala kuvitumikia. Kwa maana ndimi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, Mungu mwenye wivu. Ninaleta hatia ya baba juu ya watoto wao, juu ya vizazi vya tatu na vya nne vya wale wanaonichukia,
sw.R: Usiziinamie sanamu hizo wala kuzitumikia. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} ni Mungu mwenye wivu. Sitakubali uaminifu wako ugawanywe na miungu mingine. Watu wanaponichukia, ninaiadhibu dhambi yao, hata kwa wajukuu wao na vitukuu vyao.

ko.L: 너는 그것들에게 절하지 말고 그것들을 섬기지 말라. 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 너의 하나님은 질투하는 하나님이어서, 나를 미워하는 자들의 아버지들의 죄악을 자녀들에게, 삼 대와 사 대까지 갚는다.
ko.B: 너는 그것들에게 절하지도 말고 섬기지도 말라. 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 너의 하나님은 질투하는 하나님이다. 나를 미워하는 사람들에게는 아버지들의 죄악을 그 자녀들에게 갚되, 삼 대와 사 대까지 갚는다.
ko.R: 우상에게 절하거나 우상을 섬기면 안 된다. 나는 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}이고, 질투하는 하나님이다. 나는 네 충성을 다른 신들과 나누지 않는다. 사람들이 나를 미워하면, 나는 그들의 죄를 벌하고, 그 벌이 그들의 손자와 증손자에게까지 미치게 한다.

vi.L: Ngươi chớ quỳ lạy chúng và chớ phụng sự chúng; vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, [là] Đức Chúa Trời kỵ tà, phạt [tội] gian ác của cha trên con cái, đến [đời] thứ ba và [đời] thứ tư của những kẻ ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}},
vi.B: Ngươi không được quỳ lạy hay phụng sự chúng, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, là Đức Chúa Trời kỵ tà. Ta phạt tội của cha ông trên con cháu đến đời thứ ba và thứ tư của những kẻ ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}},
vi.R: Đừng quỳ lạy hay phục vụ chúng. Ta là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, Đức Chúa Trời kỵ tà. Ta không để ngươi chia lòng trung thành với các thần khác. Khi người ta ghét {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} phạt tội của họ, ngay cả trên con cháu và chắt chít họ.

decisions.choice: jealous: passionate, demanding sole loyalty
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:5: a burning claim on one who belongs to you, like a husband's claim on his wife's faithfulness, not petty envy (4:24; 6:15).

decisions.choice: visiting iniquity to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me: judgment that reaches a family that keeps hating God
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:5. Three or four generations could live in one household, so the sin of its head reached all who lived under it. The law did not punish children for their parents' crimes in court (24:16). Here the Hebrew adds "and" before "the third", which does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: serve them: the verb has an unusual form
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:5, the vowels give a form that may mean "be led into serving them". The sense is the same: Israel must not worship idols.

decisions.choice: grandchildren and great-grandchildren
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:5: counting the fathers as the first generation, the third and fourth are their grandchildren and great-grandchildren. Readable also adds "I will not share your loyalty" to explain "jealous".

decisions.choice: "kỵ tà"
decisions.reason: The word settled for these books (see 4:24); a passion that demands sole loyalty (meaning decision). Exodus 20:5 uses the same word.

decisions.choice: "gian ác" (L); "tội" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's words for iniquity.

source.text: וְעֹ֥שֶׂהחֶ֖סֶדלַֽאֲלָפִ֑יםלְאֹהֲבַ֖י וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And doing covenant loyalty to thousands, to those who love me and to those who keep my commandments.

en.L: and doing steadfast love to thousands, to those who love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and to those who keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments.
en.B: but to thousands who love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments I show faithful love.
en.R: But to thousands who love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands, I show faithful love.

es.L: y que obra con amor fiel hacia millares, hacia los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} aman y hacia los que guardan {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mandamientos.
es.B: pero a millares de los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} aman y cumplen {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mandamientos les muestro {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} amor fiel.
es.R: Pero muestro {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} amor fiel a miles de personas que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} aman y obedecen {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mandatos.

fr.L: et qui agit avec amour fidèle envers des milliers, envers ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aiment et envers ceux qui gardent {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements.
fr.B: mais à des milliers de ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aiment et gardent {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements, je montre un amour fidèle.
fr.R: Mais je reste fidèle dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} amour envers des milliers de gens qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aiment et qui obéissent à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements.

sw.L: na ninayefanya upendo usiokoma kwa maelfu, kwa wale wanaonipenda na kwa wale wanaozishika amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}.
sw.B: lakini maelfu ya wale wanaonipenda na kutii amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} ninawaonyesha upendo wa uaminifu.
sw.R: Lakini maelfu ya watu wanaonipenda na kufuata amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, ninawapenda kwa uaminifu bila kukoma.

ko.L: 그러나 나를 사랑하고 내 계명을 지키는 자들에게는 천 대까지 한결같은 사랑을 베푼다.
ko.B: 그러나 나를 사랑하고 내 계명을 지키는 사람들에게는 수천 대에 이르기까지 한결같은 사랑을 베푼다.
ko.R: 그러나 나를 사랑하고 내 명령을 지키는 사람들에게는 수천 대에 이르기까지 변함없는 사랑을 보여 준다.

vi.L: và làm ơn [bằng] tình yêu thương thành tín cho đến hàng ngàn [người], cho những người yêu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và những người giữ các điều răn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tỏ tình yêu thương thành tín cho hàng ngàn người yêu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và giữ các điều răn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Nhưng với hàng ngàn người yêu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và vâng giữ các điều răn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tỏ tình thương thành tín của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

decisions.choice: my commandments: the reading the Hebrew text marks to be read
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text spell "his commandments", while the scribes' note in the margin says to read "my commandments", as in Exodus 20:6. The source data follows the marked reading. "His" would refer to God in the third person in the middle of God's own speech; "my" fits the context.

decisions.choice: thousands: thousands of people, or the thousandth generation
decisions.reason: Set against "the third and the fourth" generation in verse 9, the word may mean thousands of generations, as 7:9 says ("to a thousand generations"). Either way God's love far outlasts his judgment.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal love that keeps covenant
decisions.reason: Kindness that stays true to a bond and acts on it (7:9, 12; Exodus 20:6; 34:6-7). Loving God is shown by keeping what he commands (6:5-6; 11:1).

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:6. Both stress loyalty; words such as "mercy" or "kindness" leave the loyalty out.

decisions.choice: "한결같은 사랑" (Literal, Balanced) and "변함없는 사랑" (Readable) for hesed
decisions.reason: As the Genesis and Psalms sheets set for hesed in Korean, and as the Korean Exodus 20:6 has it.

decisions.choice: "tình yêu thương thành tín" (L, B), "tình thương thành tín" (R); "hàng ngàn [người]"
decisions.reason: The forms the Genesis and Psalms notes give for hesed, loyal love that keeps covenant (meaning decision). The Hebrew says only "thousands", of people or of generations; Literal supplies "người" in brackets and the meaning decision gives the other reading.

source.text: לֹ֥א תִשָּׂ֛א אֶת־שֵֽׁם־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לַשָּׁ֑וְא כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יְנַקֶּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־יִשָּׂ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ לַשָּֽׁוְא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall lift up [the] name of Yahweh your God to emptiness, for not will leave unpunished Yahweh [the one] who lifts up his name to emptiness.

en.L: You shall not lift up the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God to emptiness, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not leave unpunished [the one] who lifts up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name to emptiness.
en.B: You shall not use the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God for what is false or worthless, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not let anyone go unpunished who uses {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name that way.
en.R: Do not use the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in false promises or for empty purposes. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will punish anyone who treats {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name like that.

es.L: No alzarás el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios para la vanidad, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no declarará inocente al que alce {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre para la vanidad.
es.B: No usarás el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios para la mentira o para lo que no vale nada, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no dejará sin castigo a nadie que use así {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.R: No uses el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios en promesas falsas ni para cosas sin valor. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} castigará a cualquiera que trate {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre de esa manera.

fr.L: Tu ne lèveras pas le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu pour le vide, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne tiendra pas pour innocent celui qui lève {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom pour le vide.
fr.B: Tu n’utiliseras pas le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu pour le mensonge ou pour rien, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne laissera sans punition personne qui se sert ainsi de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.
fr.R: N’utilise pas le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu dans de fausses promesses ou pour des choses vaines. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} punira toute personne qui traite {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom de cette façon.

sw.L: Hutaliinua jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako kwa ubatili, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatamwacha bila adhabu yule aliinuaye jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} kwa ubatili.
sw.B: Hutalitumia jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako kwa uongo au kwa mambo yasiyo na maana, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatamwachilia mtu yeyote anayelitumia jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} hivyo bila kumwadhibu.
sw.R: Usilitumie jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako katika ahadi za uongo au kwa mambo yasiyo na faida. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamwadhibu kila mtu anayelitendea jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} hivyo.

ko.L: 너는 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 이름을 헛되이 들어 올리지 말라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그분의 이름을 헛되이 들어 올리는 자를 벌하지 않고 두지 않으실 것이다.
ko.B: 너는 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 이름을 거짓되거나 헛된 일에 쓰지 말라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그분의 이름을 그렇게 쓰는 사람을 벌하지 않고 그냥 두지 않으신다.
ko.R: 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 이름을 거짓 약속이나 쓸데없는 일에 쓰면 안 된다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그분의 이름을 그렇게 함부로 쓰는 사람을 반드시 벌하신다.

vi.L: Ngươi chớ lấy danh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi mà dùng cách hư không, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ không để cho [kẻ] lấy danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà dùng cách hư không khỏi bị phạt.
vi.B: Ngươi không được dùng danh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi vào việc giả dối hay vô ích, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ không để cho ai dùng danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như thế mà khỏi bị phạt.
vi.R: Đừng dùng danh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi để hứa dối hay vào những việc vô nghĩa. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ phạt bất cứ ai coi thường danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như thế.

decisions.choice: lift up the name to emptiness: use God's name falsely or for nothing
decisions.reason: The same words as Exodus 20:7. To "lift up" the name is to speak it, above all in an oath (6:13; 10:20). "Emptiness" means what is false or worthless; verse 20 uses the same word of a witness. The command forbids swearing falsely by God's name and any use of it that treats it as empty.

decisions.choice: will not leave unpunished: will not acquit
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare clean or innocent. God will treat the one who misuses his name as guilty (Exodus 34:7).

decisions.choice: for what is false or worthless / in false promises or for empty purposes
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:7, Balanced and Readable spell out both senses of "emptiness". Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: "lấy danh ... mà dùng cách hư không" (L)
decisions.reason: "lift up the name to emptiness" (meaning decision): Literal keeps "lấy" (take up) and "hư không" (emptiness); Balanced and Readable say what the misuse is, as the English does.

source.text: שָׁמ֛וֹראֶת־י֥וֹםהַשַׁבָּ֖תלְקַדְּשׁ֑וֹכַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוְּךָ֖יְהוָ֥האֱלֹהֶֽיךָ

records.literal_gloss: Keep the day of the Sabbath to make it holy, as commanded you Yahweh your God.

en.L: Keep the day of the Sabbath, to make it holy, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded you.
en.B: Keep the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded you.
en.R: Keep the Sabbath day. Treat it as a holy day, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded you.

es.L: Guarda el día del sábado, para hacerlo santo, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te ha mandado.
es.B: Guarda el día sábado y apártalo como santo, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te lo ha ordenado.
es.R: Guarda el sábado. Trátalo como un día santo, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te ha mandado.

fr.L: Garde le jour du sabbat, pour le rendre saint, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te l’a commandé.
fr.B: Garde le jour du sabbat et mets-le à part comme saint, ainsi que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te l’a ordonné.
fr.R: Garde le jour du sabbat. Traite-le comme un jour saint : c’est ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a commandé.

sw.L: Shika siku ya Sabato, ili kuifanya takatifu, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alivyokuamuru.
sw.B: Ishike siku ya Sabato na uitenge iwe takatifu, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alivyokuamuru.
sw.R: Ishike siku ya Sabato. Iheshimu kama siku takatifu, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alivyokuagiza.

ko.L: 안식일, 그날을 지켜 그것을 거룩하게 하라. 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에게 명령하신 대로 하라.
ko.B: 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에게 명령하신 대로 안식일을 지키고, 그날을 거룩한 날로 구별하라.
ko.R: 안식일을 지켜야 한다. 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에게 명령하신 대로 그날을 거룩한 날로 지켜야 한다.

vi.L: Hãy giữ ngày Sa-bát để làm cho nó nên thánh, như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi đã truyền cho ngươi.

decisions.choice: keep: in place of "remember" in Exodus 20:8
decisions.reason: Exodus 20:8 begins "Remember the day of the Sabbath". Here the verb is "keep": to guard, watch over and carry out. It is the verb of verses 1, 10 and 29 and of the Sabbath law in Exodus 31:13-16. The two verbs do not disagree: to remember the day is to keep it. "Remember" comes back in verse 15, where Israel is to remember its slavery in Egypt.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh your God commanded you: pointing back to Horeb
decisions.reason: These words are not in Exodus 20:8. Moses is retelling the ten words forty years later, and he reminds the people that the command was already given at Horeb. The same words are added to the command about parents (verse 16).

decisions.choice: make it holy: set the day apart for God
decisions.reason: The day is to be treated as different from other days, belonging to Yahweh (Exodus 16:23; 20:8; 31:14).

decisions.choice: Keep
decisions.reason: "Keep" at every level, the same word used for keeping the commandments in verses 1, 10 and 29, so the reader can see the link.

decisions.choice: "Guarda" at every level (Exodus 20:8 "Recuerda")
decisions.reason: The same verb as "guardar" the commandments in verses 10 and 29, as the English keeps "Keep".

decisions.choice: "Garde" at every level (Exodus 20:8 "Souviens-toi")
decisions.reason: As the English keeps "Keep": the same verb as "garder" the commandments in verses 10 and 29, so the French reader sees the link and the difference from Exodus.

decisions.choice: "Shika" / "Ishike" at every level (Exodus 20:8 "Kumbuka")
decisions.reason: The same verb as "kuzishika" the commandments in verses 10 and 29, as the English keeps "Keep".

decisions.choice: "지키다" for "keep", where Exodus 20:8 has "기억하다" (remember)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes the change from Exodus; Korean marks it with a different verb so the reader comparing the two lists sees it.

decisions.choice: "Hãy giữ"
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy says "keep" where Exodus 20:8 says "remember" (meaning decision); Vietnamese keeps the difference, so that a reader comparing the two lists sees it.

records.literal_gloss: And [the] day the seventh [is] a Sabbath to Yahweh your God; not you shall do any work, you and your son and your daughter and your male slave and your female slave and your ox and your donkey and all your livestock and your sojourner who [is] in your gates, so that may rest your male slave and your female slave like you.

en.L: but the seventh day [is] a Sabbath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not do any work, you and your son and your daughter, and your male slave and your female slave, and your ox and your donkey and all your livestock, and your sojourner who [is] within your gates, so that your male slave and your female slave may rest like you.
en.B: but the seventh day is a Sabbath for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do no work on it: not you, nor your son or daughter, nor your male or female servant, nor your ox or your donkey or any of your livestock, nor the foreigner living among you in your towns, so that your male and female servants may rest as you do.
en.R: But the seventh day is a Sabbath, a day of rest for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. On that day no one in your household may work: not you, not your sons or daughters, not your servants, not your ox or donkey or any of your animals, and not the foreigners who live among you in your towns. Then your servants can rest, just as you do.

es.L: pero el día séptimo [es] sábado para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios. No harás ningún trabajo, tú y tu hijo y tu hija, y tu esclavo y tu esclava, y tu buey y tu asno y todo tu ganado, y tu inmigrante que [está] dentro de tus puertas, para que descansen tu esclavo y tu esclava como tú.
es.B: pero el séptimo día es un sábado para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios. es.R: Pero el séptimo día es el sábado, el día de descanso para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios. Ese día nadie en tu casa debe trabajar: ni tú, ni tus hijos o hijas, ni tus siervos, ni tu buey o tu burro, ni ninguno de tus animales, ni los extranjeros que viven contigo en tus ciudades. Ainsi tes serviteurs pourront se reposer, tout comme toi.

ko.L: 그러나 일곱째 날은 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 안식일이다. 너는 아무 일도 하지 말라. 너와 네 아들과 네 딸과 네 남종과 네 여종과 네 소와 네 나귀와 네 모든 가축과 네 성문 안에 있는 네 나그네도 [그러하다]. 그리하여 네 남종과 네 여종도 너처럼 쉬게 하라.
ko.B: 그러나 일곱째 날은 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 바친 안식일이다. 그날에는 아무 일도 하지 말라. 너도, 네 아들이나 딸도, 네 남종이나 여종도, 네 소나 나귀나 그 밖의 어떤 가축도, 네 성읍 안에서 함께 사는 나그네도 일해서는 안 된다. 그래야 네 남종과 여종도 너처럼 쉴 수 있다.
ko.R: 그러나 일곱째 날은 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 안식일, 곧 쉬는 날이다. 그날에는 네 집안의 누구도 일하면 안 된다. 너도, 네 아들딸도, 네 종들도, 네 소나 나귀나 그 어떤 짐승도, 네 성읍에서 함께 사는 나그네도 일하면 안 된다. 그래야 네 종들도 너처럼 쉴 수 있다.

vi.L: nhưng ngày thứ bảy [là] ngày Sa-bát cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi. Ngươi chớ làm bất cứ công việc nào, ngươi, con trai ngươi, con gái ngươi, đầy tớ nam ngươi, đầy tớ nữ ngươi, bò ngươi, lừa ngươi, mọi súc vật ngươi, và ngoại kiều ở trong các cổng thành ngươi, để đầy tớ nam và đầy tớ nữ của ngươi được nghỉ ngơi như ngươi.
vi.B: nhưng ngày thứ bảy là ngày Sa-bát dành cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi. Ngày ấy ngươi không được làm công việc gì: không phải ngươi, không phải con trai hay con gái ngươi, không phải đầy tớ nam hay đầy tớ nữ của ngươi, không phải bò, lừa hay bất cứ súc vật nào của ngươi, cũng không phải ngoại kiều sống trong các thành của ngươi, để đầy tớ nam và đầy tớ nữ của ngươi cũng được nghỉ ngơi như ngươi.
vi.R: Nhưng ngày thứ bảy là ngày Sa-bát, một ngày nghỉ dành cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi. Ngày ấy không ai trong nhà ngươi được làm việc: không phải ngươi, không phải con trai con gái ngươi, không phải đầy tớ ngươi, không phải bò, lừa hay bất cứ con vật nào của ngươi, và cũng không phải những người nước ngoài sống giữa ngươi trong các thành của ngươi. Như vậy đầy tớ ngươi cũng được nghỉ ngơi như ngươi.

decisions.choice: your ox and your donkey ... so that your servants may rest like you: additions to Exodus 20:10
decisions.reason: Exodus 20:10 says "your livestock". Here the ox and the donkey, the animals that did the heaviest work, are named first, and "all your livestock" follows. The verse also gives a purpose that Exodus does not state: the rest is so that those who serve the household may rest just as its master does. Verse 15 gives the reason.

decisions.choice: male slave, female slave: workers owned by the household
decisions.reason: The words name men and women who belonged to the household and worked for it, owned, not hired (15:12-18; Exodus 21:2-11). The command is spoken to the head of the household, who must give the day to them as to himself.

decisions.choice: your sojourner within your gates: a foreigner living in your towns
decisions.reason: A sojourner is an outsider who has settled among Israel without land or family rights (10:18-19; 24:14). "Within your gates" means inside your town.

decisions.choice: male slave, female slave (Literal); servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The usual rule for this word: "slave" at Literal, "servant" at Balanced and Readable, with m2 saying what their position was. In verse 15, where Israel's own slavery in Egypt is the point, every level says "slave". Exodus 20:10 has "servant" at Literal for the same words; Deuteronomy follows the style guide here, so the Literal wording of the two Decalogues differs while the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the foreigner(s) living among you
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:10, Balanced and Readable say "foreigner living among you"; Literal keeps "sojourner". Readable also adds "a day of rest" to explain the word Sabbath.

decisions.choice: ton esclave homme et ton esclave femme (L); ton serviteur et ta servante (B, R)
decisions.reason: French "esclave" is the same for a man and a woman, so Literal adds "homme" and "femme" to keep the Hebrew pair apart. Balanced and Readable say "serviteur" and "servante", as the English says "servant".

decisions.choice: "남종" and "여종" (Readable "종들") for the male and female slaves of the household
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "종" for household servants and "노예" for slavery itself, as in Egypt in the next verse; the Korean Exodus 20:10 uses the same words.

decisions.choice: "đầy tớ nam", "đầy tớ nữ"; "ngoại kiều" (L, B), "người nước ngoài sống giữa ngươi" (R)
decisions.reason: Workers owned by the household (meaning decision); the term sheet keeps "đầy tớ" for them, as Exodus 20:10 does, and "nô lệ" for Israel's slavery in Egypt in verse 15.

records.literal_gloss: And you shall remember that a slave you were in [the] land of Egypt, and brought you out Yahweh your God from there with a hand strong and with an arm outstretched; therefore commanded you Yahweh your God to do the day of the Sabbath.

en.L: And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm; therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded you to observe the day of the Sabbath.
en.B: Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God led you out from there by a strong hand and an outstretched arm. For this reason {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.
en.R: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power to bring you out of there. That is why {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.

es.L: Y recordarás que eras esclavo en la tierra de Egipto, y que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te hizo salir de allí con mano fuerte y con brazo extendido; por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te ordenó observar el día del sábado.
es.B: Recuerda que eras esclavo en el país de Egipto y que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te sacó de allí con mano poderosa y brazo extendido. Por esa razón {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te ha ordenado observar el día sábado.
es.R: Recuerda que eras esclavo en Egipto, y que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios usó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gran poder para sacarte de allí. Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te ha mandado guardar el sábado.

fr.L: Et tu te rappelleras que tu étais esclave dans le pays d’Égypte, et que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a fait sortir de là par une main forte et par un bras étendu ; c’est pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a commandé d’observer le jour du sabbat.
fr.B: Souviens-toi que tu étais esclave au pays d’Égypte, et que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a fait sortir de là d’une main puissante et d’un bras étendu. Voilà pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a ordonné d’observer le jour du sabbat.
fr.R: Souviens-toi que tu étais esclave en Égypte, et que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu s’est servi de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grande puissance pour t’en faire sortir. C’est pour cela que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a commandé de garder le jour du sabbat.

sw.L: Nawe utakumbuka ya kuwa wewe ulikuwa mtumwa katika nchi ya Misri, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alikutoa kutoka huko kwa mkono wenye nguvu na kwa mkono ulionyooshwa; ndiyo sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako amekuamuru kuiadhimisha siku ya Sabato.
sw.B: Kumbuka kwamba ulikuwa mtumwa katika nchi ya Misri, na kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alikuleta nje kutoka huko kwa mkono hodari na kwa mkono ulionyooshwa. Kwa sababu hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako amekuamuru uiadhimishe siku ya Sabato.
sw.R: Kumbuka kwamba ulikuwa mtumwa huko Misri, na kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alitumia nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} kuu kukutoa huko. Ndiyo maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako amekuamuru uishike siku ya Sabato.

decisions.choice: remember that you were a slave in Egypt: a different reason from Exodus 20:11
decisions.reason: In Exodus 20:11 the reason for the Sabbath is creation: God made the world in six days and rested on the seventh. Here the reason is the rescue from Egypt. A people once worked as slaves without rest, and set free by God, must give rest to those who work for them (verse 14; 15:15; 16:12; 24:18, 22). The two reasons stand side by side; neither cancels the other.

decisions.choice: a strong hand and an outstretched arm: God's power shown in the rescue
decisions.reason: The hand and the arm are pictures of strength in action. The pair describes the plagues and the crossing of the sea (4:34; 7:19; 26:8; Exodus 6:6).

decisions.choice: to do the day of the Sabbath: to observe it, to hold it as it should be held
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary word "do". With a festival or a holy day it means to keep or celebrate it (Exodus 31:16; Deuteronomy 16:1, 10).

decisions.choice: slave(s) at every level
decisions.reason: This is Israel's own slavery in Egypt, so "slave" stays at every level; the contrast with the servants of verse 14 is the point of the verse.

decisions.choice: used his great power
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the hand and the arm (m2).

decisions.choice: "tu étais esclave" (singular) at every level; "observer" (L, B), "garder" (R) the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks to Israel as one ("you were a slave"), and French follows the Hebrew number even where the English Readable says "slaves". "Faire" the Sabbath (m3) is said "observer"; Readable uses "garder", as the English Readable says "keep".

decisions.choice: "강한 손과 편 팔" for "a strong hand and an outstretched arm"; Readable "큰 능력"
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture, which recurs through Deuteronomy; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

records.literal_gloss: Honor your father and your mother, as commanded you Yahweh your God, so that may be long your days and so that it may go well with you on the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you.

en.L: Honor your father and your mother, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded you, so that your days may be long, and so that it may go well with you upon the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving to you.
en.B: Honor your father and your mother, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you. Then your days will be long, and it will go well with you in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is going to give you.
en.R: Honor your father and your mother, and treat them with respect, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you. Then you will enjoy a long life, and things will go well for you in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is about to give you.

es.R: Honra a tu padre y a tu madre, y trátalos con respeto, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te ha mandado. Así vivirás muchos años, y te irá bien en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios está a punto de darte.

fr.R: Honore ton père et ta mère, et traite-les avec respect, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te l’a commandé. Alors tu profiteras d’une longue vie, et tout ira bien pour toi dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu est sur le point de te donner.

vi.R: Hãy hiếu kính cha mẹ ngươi và tôn trọng họ, như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi đã truyền cho ngươi. Như vậy ngươi sẽ được sống lâu, và mọi việc sẽ tốt đẹp cho ngươi trong xứ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi sắp ban cho ngươi.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh commanded you ... and so that it may go well with you: additions to Exodus 20:12
decisions.reason: Exodus 20:12 promises long life in the land. Here the command again points back to Horeb (as in verse 12), and a second promise is added: "that it may go well with you", a phrase Deuteronomy uses often (4:40; 6:3, 18; 22:7). Ephesians 6:2-3 quotes the command with this added promise.

decisions.choice: honor: give weight to, respect and care for
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:12. To honor parents is to treat them as weighty: to respect, obey and care for them all their lives (21:18-21; 27:16).

decisions.choice: the land: the ground of Canaan that God is giving
decisions.reason: The word is the one for soil and farmland. The promise is a long and good life in the land Israel is about to enter (4:40; 11:9).

decisions.choice: "hiếu kính"
decisions.reason: To honor is to respect and care for (meaning decision); "hiếu kính" is that duty of a child to parents, as in Exodus 20:12.

decisions.choice: murder: the unlawful killing of a person
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:13. This verb is used only of killing a human being, by intent or by careless violence (4:41-42; 19:4-6; Numbers 35:16-21), and never of killing in battle. The law itself sets the death penalty for some crimes (19:11-13), so the command forbids unlawful killing.

decisions.choice: the verse division follows the source data
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20, the Hebrew text of the ten words carries two sets of accents, and Hebrew Bibles that follow the second set may join verses 17-20 into a single verse. The source data numbers them as four verses, so the verse numbers of this chapter are the same as in the usual numbering of translations, and no shift in numbering needs to be noted here.

decisions.choice: and: the last commands are joined into one chain
decisions.reason: In Exodus 20:14-17 each of the last four commands stands on its own. Here each begins with "and" (verses 18-21), linking them as one series of duties toward one's neighbor.

decisions.choice: commit adultery: sexual union that breaks a marriage
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:14: sexual relations between a married or betrothed woman and a man who is not her husband, and both were guilty (22:22-24).

decisions.choice: no "and" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "And" at the start of verses 18-21 to show the chain (m1); in Balanced and Readable a list of commands reads more naturally without it.

decisions.choice: a witness of emptiness: in place of "a witness of falsehood" in Exodus 20:16
decisions.reason: Exodus 20:16 has the word for a lie. Here the word is "emptiness", the same as in verse 11 ("lift up the name to emptiness"): testimony that is groundless, worthless, false. It forbids not only an outright lie but any evidence with nothing behind it. The use of the same word links misuse of God's name and misuse of a neighbor's case.

decisions.choice: answer as a witness: testify in court
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:16, to "answer" is the word for giving evidence in a case. A false witness was to suffer what he meant to bring on the other (19:16-19).

decisions.choice: neighbor: a fellow member of the community
decisions.reason: The word means the person beside you: a fellow Israelite, anyone you deal with.

decisions.choice: baseless evidence / false or empty things
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the difference from Exodus 20:16 (m1): the testimony is empty, without ground. Literal keeps "a witness of emptiness".

decisions.choice: testigo de vanidad (L); un testimonio sin fundamento (B)
decisions.reason: Literal uses the same word as "para la vanidad" in verse 11, not the "mentira" of Exodus 20:16.

decisions.choice: témoin de vide (L); un témoignage sans fondement (B)
decisions.reason: Literal uses the same word as "pour le vide" in verse 11, so the link between the two commands shows, and not the "mensonge" of Exodus 20:16.

decisions.choice: shahidi wa ubatili (L); ushahidi usio na msingi (B)
decisions.reason: Literal uses the same word as "kwa ubatili" in verse 11, not the "uongo" of Exodus 20:16.

decisions.choice: "헛된 증인" (Literal), "근거 없는 증언" (Balanced) for "a witness of emptiness"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that this differs from "a witness of falsehood" in Exodus 20:16, where the Korean has "거짓"; Korean keeps the difference.

decisions.choice: "hư không" (L); "vô căn cứ" (B)
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy says "a witness of emptiness" where Exodus 20:16 says "of falsehood" (meaning decision); Literal keeps "hư không", and Balanced "vô căn cứ", testimony with nothing behind it.

en.L: And you shall not covet the wife of your neighbor; and you shall not desire the house of your neighbor, his field, or his male slave, or his female slave, his ox, or his donkey, or anything that [belongs] to your neighbor.'
